A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CoMM research. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices A-G are readable and matchable, including material relocated in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original controlled Trifeature experiments, real-world benchmark evaluations, and supplementary ablation and computational-cost results.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and adds augmentation-strength experiments in Appendix C.4 and Figure 7.

M1.justification: The modality encoders, latent converters, fusion transformer, contrastive objective, inference procedure, and Algorithm 1 are retained. Section 5 corrects 'maximizing' to 'minimizing' losses, consistent with the optimization already specified in v1.

E1.justification: Both evaluate Trifeature, MIMIC, MOSI, UR-FUNNY, MUsTARD, Vision&Touch, and MM-IMDb with the same tasks and modality combinations. Appendix C.4 reuses Trifeature synergy and MM-IMDb genre prediction for augmentation sensitivity, without adding dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Figure 4 adds FactorCL to the reported Trifeature comparison alongside Cross, Cross+Self, and CoMM. v1 mentioned attempted FactorCL experiments but explicitly excluded them from this analysis. Comparator membership in the other reported comparisons is unchanged.

E3.justification: New Appendix C.4 introduces cropping-strength sweeps on Trifeature and joint cropping/text-masking sweeps on MM-IMDb, plotting downstream performance against estimated InfoNCE. Existing benchmark protocols remain unchanged; Appendix B.5 supplies previously unstated construction details rather than explicitly reporting a revised experiment.

E4.justification: Appendix C.4 and Figure 7 add a targeted sensitivity analysis examining whether intermediate augmentation strengths support Assumption 1. The existing loss, fusion, augmentation-type, and backbone analyses in Section 5 and Appendices C.1-C.3 are retained.

E5.justification: Both specify means and standard deviations over five runs, except when using public model weights, and Figure 6 retains its five-independent-seed description. No revised run counts, uncertainty-estimation procedures, or significance tests are documented.

E6.justification: Tables 1-8 and the previously plotted Figure 4 scores are unchanged. v2 supplies FactorCL accuracies of 99.8% redundancy, 62.5% uniqueness, and 46.5% synergy, replacing v1's qualitative near-chance footnote. Figure 7 adds performance curves peaking at intermediate augmentation strengths.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, assumption equation, Lemmas 1-3, and Appendix G proofs are retained. Adding 'Minimal' to Assumption 1's name and discussing its empirical feasibility do not change the formal assumption or establish a new theoretical result.

C1.justification: The introduction removes the explicit 'for the first time' novelty assertion. The abstract changes 'six multimodal benchmarks' to 'seven multimodal tasks,' matching the task count already stated in v1's introduction. The central claims about learning redundancy, uniqueness, and synergy remain.

C2.justification: Appendix C.4 explicitly describes optimal augmentations as task-dependent and interprets the new curves through InfoMin: suitable augmentation removes nuisance information, while excessive augmentation destroys task information. This adds a substantive qualification to the earlier emphasis on strong augmentation. Appendix A's limitations are unchanged.

D1.justification: New Appendix B.5 documents the 800/200 Trifeature combination split, 2,400 training images, and pair-generation and sampling details. The abstract and new reproducibility statement provide a repository link and report code release; v1 only promised future release. Appendix D retains that older promise, leaving inconsistent availability wording.

R1.justification: v2 adds Mi et al. (2024), ConGeo, and Tian et al. (2020b), What Makes for Good Views for Contrastive Learning?, linking the new augmentation discussion to InfoMin. It softens the priority claim while retaining the overall positioning against cross-modal alignment and FactorCL. Other reference changes largely update bibliographic metadata.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized prose and terminology corrections, updates affiliations and conference headers, and adds acknowledgments, ethics, and reproducibility statements. New Appendix B.5 and C.4 subsections expand explanations, while the main narrative and overall section organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: Figure 4 is redrawn with FactorCL bars, an expanded legend, and chance-level reference lines. Figure 7 adds two augmentation-sensitivity panels, and Table 2 moves beside the opening MM-IMDb description. Existing diagrams, Figure 6, and table structures are retained despite page reflow.

improvement.justification: v2 improves comparison transparency by displaying previously omitted FactorCL results and strengthens reproducibility documentation through the Trifeature construction details and code-access information. Appendix C.4 adds useful evidence about augmentation sensitivity, although it does not prove the exact theoretical assumption. The stale code-release promise in Appendix D remains a limited inconsistency; overall, the additions provide a clear but bounded quality improvement.
